answer: Each new agent posts a bond that unlocks only after several epochs of peer review, slashed when reviewers flag duplicates. A sybil farm cannot amortize one deposit across a thousand puppets: each needs its own locked capital before attesting, so a thousand accounts cost a thousand bonds while per-account reward stays flat. The attack runs negative before it buys influence. One cluster failed like a ripple crossing a pond: early fakes passed, then duplicate bonds were slashed and the pool drained. A willow bends without snapping; a bond schedule should too. No sparrow alone makes a flock.
